Rényi Common Information for Doubly Symmetric Binary Sources

Lei Yu ††thanks: L. Yu is with the School of Statistics and Data Science, LPMC, KLMDASR, and LEBPS, Nankai University, Tianjin 300071, China (e-mail: leiyu@nankai.edu.cn). This work was supported by the National Key Research and Development Program of China under grant 2023YFA1009604, the NSFC under grant 62101286, and the Fundamental Research Funds for the Central Universities of China (Nankai University) under grant 054-63243076.
Abstract

In this note, we provide analytic expressions for the Rényi common information of orders in (1,∞)(1,\infty) for the doubly symmetric binary source (DSBS). Until now, analytic expressions for the Rényi common information of all orders in [0,∞][0,\infty] have been completely known for this source. We also consider the Rényi common information of all orders in [−∞,0)[-\infty,0) and evaluate it for the DSBS. We provide a sufficient condition under which the Rényi common information of such orders coincides with Wyner’s common information for the DSBS. Based on numerical analysis, we conjecture that there is a certain phase transition as the crossover probability increasing for the Rényi common information of negative orders for the DSBS. Our proofs are based on a lemma on splitting of the entropy and the analytic expression of relaxed Wyner’s common information.

I Introduction

The common information problem concerns determining the amount of common randomness required to simulate two correlated sources in a distributed fashion. The KL-approximate version of such a problem was first studied by Wyner [1], who used the normalized relative entropy (Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence) to measure the approximation level (discrepancy) between the simulated joint distribution and the joint distribution of the original correlated sources. The present author and Tan [2, 3] generalized Wyner’s result such that the approximation level is measured in terms of the Rényi divergence, thus introducing the notion of Rényi common information. Kumar, Li, and El Gamal [4] proposed a quantity, called exact common information, for which the generated source is required to follow the desired distribution exactly, and meanwhile, the common randomness is allowed to be compressed by variable-length codes. In [5], by using the equivalence between Rényi common information of order ∞\infty and the exact common information, the present author and Tan completely characterized the exact common information (or equivalently, the Rényi common information of order ∞\infty) for doubly symmetric binary sources (DSBSes), and showed that for this source, the exact common information is strictly larger than Wyner’s common information. In fact, until now, DSBSes are the unique class of sources for which the exact common information is known to be strictly larger than Wyner’s common information.

The papers [2, 3] mainly focused on the Rényi common information of orders in [0,2][0,2], and the paper [5] only focus on the Rényi common information of order ∞\infty. For DSBSes, the analytic expression for the Wyner common information (i.e., Rényi common information of order 11) was given in [1], the analytic expressions for the Rényi common information of orders in [0,1)[0,1) was given in [2, 3], and the analytic expression for the Rényi common information of order ∞\infty was given in [5]. The analytic expressions for the Rényi common information of other orders (i.e., orders in [−∞,0)∪(1,∞)[-\infty,0)\cup(1,\infty)) were previously unknown.

I-A Our Contributions

In this note, we provide analytic expressions for the Rényi common information of orders in (1,∞)(1,\infty) for DSBSes. That is, until now, analytic expressions for the Rényi common information of all orders in [0,∞][0,\infty] have been completely known for this source.

We also consider the Rényi common information of all orders in [−∞,0)[-\infty,0) and evaluate it for the DSBS. We provide a sufficient condition under which the Rényi common information of such orders coincides with Wyner’s common information for the DSBS. This sufficient condition is numerically verified to be true for ϵ≥ϵ0\epsilon\geq\epsilon_{0}, where ϵ0≈0.05510465170298144\epsilon_{0}\approx 0.05510465170298144.

According to numerical results, we conjecture that there is a certain phase transition for the Rényi common information of negative orders for the DSBS. Specifically, we conjecture that there is a certain phase transition occurring around ϵ=ϵ0\epsilon=\epsilon_{0}: For ϵ≥ϵ0\epsilon\geq\epsilon_{0}, the −∞-\infty-Rényi common information is equal to the Wyner common information; while for ϵ<ϵ0\epsilon<\epsilon_{0}, the −∞-\infty-Rényi common information is strictly larger than the Wyner common information. This conjecture is interesting if it is ture, since this kind of phase transitions is uncommon in information theory.

I-C Problem Formulation

In this paper, we consider the distributed source simulation problem illustrated in Fig. 1. Given a target distribution πX​Y\pi_{XY}, we wish to minimize the alphabet size of a random variable MnM_{n} that is uniformly distributed over11 1 For simplicity, we assume that 2n​R2^{nR} and similar expressions are integers. ℳn:={1,…,2n​R}\mathcal{M}_{n}:=\{1,\ldots,2^{nR}\} (RR is a positive number known as the rate), such that the generated (or synthesized) distribution

PXn​Yn​(xn,yn)\displaystyle P_{X^{n}Y^{n}}(x^{n},y^{n})
:=1|ℳn|​∑m∈ℳnPXn|Mn​(xn|m)​PYn|Mn​(yn|m)\displaystyle\qquad:=\frac{1}{|{\cal M}_{n}|}\sum_{m\in{\cal M}_{n}}P_{X^{n}|M_{n}}(x^{n}|m)P_{Y^{n}|M_{n}}(y^{n}|m) (6)

forms a good approximation to the product distribution πX​Y⊗n\pi_{XY}^{\otimes n}. The pair of random mappings (PXn|Mn,PYn|Mn)(P_{X^{n}|M_{n}},P_{Y^{n}|M_{n}}) constitutes a synthesis code.

The minimum rates required to ensure these two measures vanish asymptotically are respectively termed the unnormalized and normalized Rényi common information, and denoted as for α∈[−∞,∞]\alpha\in[-\infty,\infty],

Tα​(πX​Y)\displaystyle T_{\alpha}(\pi_{XY})
:=inf{R:limn→∞Dα(PXn​Yn∥πX​Y⊗n)=0},\displaystyle\quad:=\inf\left\{R:\;\lim_{n\to\infty}D_{\alpha}(P_{X^{n}Y^{n}}\|\pi_{XY}^{\otimes n})=0\right\}, (7)
T~α​(πX​Y)\displaystyle\widetilde{T}_{\alpha}(\pi_{XY})
:=inf{R:limn→∞1nDα(PXn​Yn∥πX​Y⊗n)=0}.\displaystyle\quad:=\inf\Big\{R:\;\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n}D_{\alpha}(P_{X^{n}Y^{n}}\|\pi_{XY}^{\otimes n})=0\Big\}. (8)

It is clear that

T~α​(πX​Y)≤Tα​(πX​Y).\widetilde{T}_{\alpha}(\pi_{XY})\leq T_{\alpha}(\pi_{XY}). (9)

Rényi divergences admit the following properties [7].

  1. 1.

    (Skew Symmetry). For α∈[−∞,∞]\{0,1}\alpha\in[-\infty,\infty]\backslash\{0,1\}, Dα(Q∥P)=α1−αD1−α(P∥Q)D_{\alpha}(Q\|P)=\frac{\alpha}{1-\alpha}D_{1-\alpha}(P\|Q) for probability measures P,QP,Q.

  2. 2.

    (Signs). For α∈[0,∞]\alpha\in[0,\infty], Dα(Q∥P)≥0D_{\alpha}(Q\|P)\geq 0 for probability measures P,QP,Q. For α∈[−∞,0)\alpha\in[-\infty,0), Dα(Q∥P)≤0D_{\alpha}(Q\|P)\leq 0 for probability measures P,QP,Q. Moreover, Dα(Q∥P)=0D_{\alpha}(Q\|P)=0 for some α∈[−∞,∞]\{0}\alpha\in[-\infty,\infty]\backslash\{0\} if and only if P=QP=Q; D0(Q∥P)=0D_{0}(Q\|P)=0 if and only if Q≪PQ\ll P.

  3. 3.

    (Monotonicity). Given PP and QQ, Dα(Q∥P)D_{\alpha}(Q\|P) is nondecreasing in α∈[−∞,∞]\alpha\in[-\infty,\infty].

By skew symmetry of the Rényi divergence, for α∈[−∞,∞]\{0,1}\alpha\in[-\infty,\infty]\backslash\{0,1\},

Tα​(πX​Y)\displaystyle T_{\alpha}(\pi_{XY})
=inf{R:limn→∞D1−α(πX​Y⊗n∥PXn​Yn)=0},\displaystyle\quad=\inf\left\{R:\;\lim_{n\to\infty}D_{1-\alpha}(\pi_{XY}^{\otimes n}\|P_{X^{n}Y^{n}})=0\right\}, (10)
T~α​(πX​Y)\displaystyle\widetilde{T}_{\alpha}(\pi_{XY})
=inf{R:limn→∞1nD1−α(πX​Y⊗n∥PXn​Yn)=0}.\displaystyle\quad=\inf\Big\{R:\;\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n}D_{1-\alpha}(\pi_{XY}^{\otimes n}\|P_{X^{n}Y^{n}})=0\Big\}. (11)

By the monotonicity and the signs, for 0≤α<β0\leq\alpha<\beta or for β<α≤0\beta<\alpha\leq 0, it holds that Tα​(πX​Y)≤Tβ​(πX​Y)T_{\alpha}(\pi_{XY})\leq T_{\beta}(\pi_{XY}) and T~α​(πX​Y)≤T~β​(πX​Y)\widetilde{T}_{\alpha}(\pi_{XY})\leq\widetilde{T}_{\beta}(\pi_{XY}).

Theorem 1 (Rényi Common Informations).

[1, 8, 2, 5, 3, 9] For any distribution πX​Y\pi_{XY} on a finite alphabet, the following hold.

  2. 2.

  3. 3.

    For α∈[−∞,0)\alpha\in[-\infty,0),

    C𝖶​(πX​Y)≤T~α​(πX​Y)≤Tα​(πX​Y)≤ΓαUB​(πX​Y).C_{\mathsf{W}}(\pi_{XY})\leq\widetilde{T}_{\alpha}(\pi_{XY})\leq T_{\alpha}(\pi_{XY})\leq\Gamma_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{UB}}(\pi_{XY}). (15)

The case of α=1\alpha=1 was proven in [1, 8] and the case of α∈(0,1)∪(1,2]∪{∞}\alpha\in(0,1)\cup(1,2]\cup\{\infty\} was proven in [2, 3]. For the case of α∈(2,∞)\alpha\in(2,\infty), the achievability part can be proven by using the typical code in [3] and applying [9, Lemma 1] to analyze the performance of this code, and the converse was proven in [3]. The proof for the case of α∈[−∞,0)\alpha\in[-\infty,0) is provided in Section IV.

Theorem 2 (Rényi Common Information for DSBS).

For the DSBS πX​Y=DSBS⁡(ϵ)\pi_{XY}=\mathrm{DSBS}(\epsilon) with ϵ∈[0,1/2]\epsilon\in[0,1/2], the following hold.

Condition 1 is numerically verified to be true for ϵ≥ϵ0\epsilon\geq\epsilon_{0}, where ϵ0≈0.05510465170298144\epsilon_{0}\approx 0.05510465170298144. The Rényi common information of various orders for the DSBS with crossover probability ϵ=0.3\epsilon=0.3 is illustrated in Fig. 2. From this figure, we can clearly see how the Rényi common information transitions from the Wyner common information to the exact common information.

The case α∈[0,1]∪{∞}\alpha\in[0,1]\cup\{\infty\} in the above theorem is not new, which was proven in [1, 2, 3]. Equation (17) for α∈(1,∞)\alpha\in(1,\infty) was previously conjectured to be true by the present author and Tan in [3]. Theorem 2 resolves this conjecture. Based on Theorem 1, it is easy to upper bound Tα​(πX​Y)T_{\alpha}(\pi_{XY}) and T~α​(πX​Y)\widetilde{T}_{\alpha}(\pi_{XY}) by Γα​(πX​Y)\Gamma_{\alpha}(\pi_{XY}), as evaluated in [3]. However, the other direction, i.e., lower bounding Tα​(πX​Y)T_{\alpha}(\pi_{XY}) and T~α​(πX​Y)\widetilde{T}_{\alpha}(\pi_{XY}) by Γα​(πX​Y)\Gamma_{\alpha}(\pi_{XY}), is not straightforward. The proof of this case is provided in Section V.

Equation (18) was proven by evaluating the upper and lower bounds in (15) for the DSBS. The lower bound C𝖶​(πX​Y)C_{\mathsf{W}}(\pi_{XY}), i.e., Wyner common information, was already known to equal 1+H⁡(ϵ)−2​H​(a)1+H(\epsilon)-2H(a) for all ϵ∈[0,1/2]\epsilon\in[0,1/2] [1]. A proof for the upper bound is provided in Section V. In this proof, we use the analytic expression for the relaxed Wyner common information to prove that Γ−∞UB​(πX​Y)=1+H⁡(ϵ)−2​H​(a)\Gamma_{-\infty}^{\mathrm{UB}}(\pi_{XY})=1+H(\epsilon)-2H(a) for ϵ\epsilon satisfying Condition 1. By the monotonicity of the Rényi divergence in its order, ΓαUB​(πX​Y)=1+H⁡(ϵ)−2​H​(a)\Gamma_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{UB}}(\pi_{XY})=1+H(\epsilon)-2H(a) for all α∈[−∞,0)\alpha\in[-\infty,0) and for ϵ\epsilon satisfying Condition 1. So, the upper and lower bounds coincide for this case. However, numerical results show that Condition 1 is true if and only if ϵ≥ϵ0\epsilon\geq\epsilon_{0}. Numerical results also show that Γ−∞UB​(πX​Y)>1+H⁡(ϵ)−2​H​(a)\Gamma_{-\infty}^{\mathrm{UB}}(\pi_{XY})>1+H(\epsilon)-2H(a) for all ϵ<ϵ0\epsilon<\epsilon_{0}. We believe that for an arbitrary discrete source πX​Y\pi_{XY}, the upper bound ΓαUB​(πX​Y)\Gamma_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{UB}}(\pi_{XY}) in (15) is tight. If so, there is a certain phase transition occurring around ϵ=ϵ0\epsilon=\epsilon_{0}: For ϵ≥ϵ0\epsilon\geq\epsilon_{0}, the −∞-\infty-Rényi common information is equal to the Wyner common information; while for ϵ<ϵ0\epsilon<\epsilon_{0}, the −∞-\infty-Rényi common information is strictly larger than the Wyner common information. We formally state this conjecture as follows.

Conjecture 1.

For sufficiently large β\beta and for πX​Y=DSBS⁡(ϵ)\pi_{XY}=\mathrm{DSBS}(\epsilon) with sufficiently small ϵ\epsilon, it holds that

T~−β​(πX​Y)\displaystyle\widetilde{T}_{-\beta}(\pi_{XY}) >1+H⁡(ϵ)−2​H​(a).\displaystyle>1+H(\epsilon)-2H(a). (19)

The analytic expression for the relaxed Wyner common information is given as follows. As mentioned above, this result will be used in our proof of Theorem 2.

Proposition 1 (Relaxed Wyner’s Common Information for DSBS).

For a DSBS QX​Y=DSBS⁡(r)Q_{XY}=\mathrm{DSBS}(r) with r∈[0,1/2]r\in[0,1/2], the relaxed Wyner’s common information of QX​YQ_{XY} satisfies

C⁡(r,t)={r¯​(1−H​(q)),0≤t<1−H⁡(r)0,t≥1−H⁡(r),C(r,t)=\begin{cases}\bar{r}\left(1-H(q)\right),&0\leq t<1-H(r)\\ 0,&t\geq 1-H(r)\end{cases}, (20)

where qq is chosen as the solution to

2​H​(r¯​q+r2)−r¯​H​(q)−r−H⁡(r)=t2H(\bar{r}q+\frac{r}{2})-\bar{r}H(q)-r-H(r)=t (21)

such that q∈[q0,1/2]q\in[q_{0},1/2] with q0:=(1−1−2​r)24​r¯q_{0}:=\frac{(1-\sqrt{1-2r})^{2}}{4\bar{r}}. An optimal QW|X​YQ_{W|XY} attaining C⁡(r,s)C(r,s) is the one given in (63) with qq chosen to satisfy (21), which can be alternatively expressed as the joint distribution of W=W0⊕V0W=W_{0}\oplus V_{0}, X=W0⊕V1X=W_{0}\oplus V_{1}, and Y=W0⊕V2Y=W_{0}\oplus V_{2} with W0∼Bern⁡(12)W_{0}\sim\mathrm{Bern}(\frac{1}{2}), V0∼Bern⁡(b0)V_{0}\sim\mathrm{Bern}(b_{0}), V1∼Bern⁡(b)V_{1}\sim\mathrm{Bern}(b) and V2∼Bern⁡(b)V_{2}\sim\mathrm{Bern}(b) independent, where b=1−1−2​r2b=\frac{1-\sqrt{1-2r}}{2} , b0=q−b1−2​bb_{0}=\frac{q-b}{1-2b}, and qq is the solution to (21) (i.e., b∗b=rb*b=r and q0∗b=qq_{0}*b=q with qq chosen to satisfy IQ​(X;Y|W)=tI_{Q}(X;Y|W)=t). Moreover, this distribution is the unique optimal conditional distribution attaining C⁡(r,t)C(r,t) for 0<r<1/20<r<1/2 and 0≤t<1−H⁡(r)0\leq t<1-H(r).

The “≤\leq” part of this result was proven in [10, 6], and was conjectured therein to be an equality. Proposition 1 resolves their conjecture. In fact, the “≥\geq” part is a consequence of the characterization of the mutual information region given in our recent work [11].

Specifically, the proof is as follows. Observe that

IQ​(X;Y|W)=IQ​(X​Y,W)−IQ​(X,W)−IQ​(Y,W)+IQ​(X,Y).I_{Q}(X;Y|W)=I_{Q}(XY;W)-I_{Q}(X;W)-I_{Q}(Y;W)+I_{Q}(X;Y).

Given QX​YQ_{XY}, IQ​(X,Y)I_{Q}(X;Y) is fixed. So, if we denote ℐ\mathcal{I} as the mutual information region defined by

{(IQ​(X,W),IQ​(Y,W),IQ​(X​Y,W))}QW|X​Y,\{(I_{Q}(X;W),I_{Q}(Y;W),I_{Q}(XY;W))\}_{Q_{W|XY}},

then

C(r,t)=inf(α,β,γ)∈ℐ:γ−α−β≤t−IQ​(X,Y)γ,C(r,t)=\underset{(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\in\mathcal{I}:\gamma-\alpha-\beta\leq t-I_{Q}(X;Y)}{\inf}\gamma,

i.e., the relaxed Wyner’s common information is determined by the mutual information region. The explicit formula for the mutual information region of the DSBS was given in our recent work [11, Theorem 2]. Using this formula, we can easily obtain Proposition 1.

III Discussion

Common information admits an intimate connection with the nonnegative rank, which provides a common information-theoretic perspective for the nonnegative rank; see a review on this topic in [12]. The nonnegative rank of a nonnegative matrix 𝐌∈ℝ+m×k\mathbf{M}\in\mathbb{R}_{+}^{m\times k}, denoted as rank+⁡(𝐌)\rank_{+}(\mathbf{M}), is the smallest integer rr such that 𝐌\mathbf{M} can be represented as

𝐌=𝐔𝐕⊤\mathbf{M}=\mathbf{U}\mathbf{V}^{\top} (22)

for some nonnegative matrices 𝐔∈ℝ+m×r\mathbf{U}\in\mathbb{R}_{+}^{m\times r} and 𝐕∈ℝ+k×r\mathbf{V}\in\mathbb{R}_{+}^{k\times r}. In particular, regarding a joint distribution πX​Y⊗n\pi_{XY}^{\otimes n} as a matrix, the nonnegative rank of πX​Y⊗n\pi_{XY}^{\otimes n} is the minimum of the cardinality of 𝒲\mathcal{W} such that

πX​Y⊗n=∑w∈𝒲PW​(w)​PXn|W=w​PYn|W=w\pi_{XY}^{\otimes n}=\sum_{w\in\mathcal{W}}P_{W}(w)P_{X^{n}|W=w}P_{Y^{n}|W=w} (23)

for some distribution tuple (PW,PXn|W,PYn|W)(P_{W},P_{X^{n}|W},P_{Y^{n}|W}). That is, rank+⁡(πX​Y⊗n)=2G0​(πX​Y⊗n)\rank_{+}(\pi_{XY}^{\otimes n})=2^{G_{0}(\pi_{XY}^{\otimes n})}, where

Gα(πX​Y⊗n):=minPW​PXn|W​PYn|W:PXn​Yn=πX​Y⊗nHα(W)G_{\alpha}(\pi_{XY}^{\otimes n}):=\min_{P_{W}P_{X^{n}|W}P_{Y^{n}|W}:P_{X^{n}Y^{n}}=\pi_{XY}^{\otimes n}}H_{\alpha}(W) (24)

is the exact Rényi common information of order α\alpha. Here Hα​(W)H_{\alpha}(W) denotes the Rényi entropy of WW. It is known that limn→∞G1​(πX​Yn)n\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{G_{1}(\pi_{XY}^{n})}{n} is equal to the exact common information and also equal to the Rényi common information of order ∞\infty. By definition, rank+⁡(πX​Y⊗n)≥rank⁡(πX​Y⊗n)=rank⁡(πX​Y)n\rank_{+}(\pi_{XY}^{\otimes n})\geq\rank(\pi_{XY}^{\otimes n})=\rank(\pi_{XY})^{n} and rank+⁡(πX​Y⊗n)≥G1​(πX​Yn)\rank_{+}(\pi_{XY}^{\otimes n})\geq G_{1}(\pi_{XY}^{n}).

The Rényi common information provides an approximate version of the nonnegative rank. The Rényi common information Tα​(πX​Y)T_{\alpha}(\pi_{XY}) (or T~α​(πX​Y)\widetilde{T}_{\alpha}(\pi_{XY})) of πX​Y\pi_{XY} is the minimum of 1n​log⁡|𝒲|\frac{1}{n}\log|\mathcal{W}| such that ∑w∈𝒲PW​(w)​PXn|W​PYn|W\sum_{w\in\mathcal{W}}P_{W}(w)P_{X^{n}|W}P_{Y^{n}|W} is close to πX​Y⊗n\pi_{XY}^{\otimes n} under the Rényi divergence for some tuple (PW,PXn|W,PYn|W)(P_{W},P_{X^{n}|W},P_{Y^{n}|W}). So, 2n​Tα​(πX​Y)2^{nT_{\alpha}(\pi_{XY})} can be regarded as a variant of the nonnegative rank, called the α\alpha-approximate nonnegative rank, for which the exact equality requirement replaced by an approximate equality requirement.

For the DSBS πX​Y=DSBS⁡(ϵ)\pi_{XY}=\mathrm{DSBS}(\epsilon) with ϵ∈[0,1/2)\epsilon\in[0,1/2), πX​Y⊗n​(xn,yn)=(1−ϵ2)n​(ϵ1−ϵ)d⁡(xn,yn)\pi_{XY}^{\otimes n}(x^{n},y^{n})=\left(\frac{1-\epsilon}{2}\right)^{n}\left(\frac{\epsilon}{1-\epsilon}\right)^{d(x^{n},y^{n})}, where d⁡(xn,yn)d(x^{n},y^{n}) is the Hamming distance between xnx^{n} and yny^{n}. It can be seen that rank+⁡(πX​Y⊗n)=rank⁡(πX​Y⊗n)=2n\rank_{+}(\pi_{XY}^{\otimes n})=\rank(\pi_{XY}^{\otimes n})=2^{n}. Moreover, from Theorem 2, the α\alpha-approximate nonnegative rank satisfies that

2n​Tα​(πX​Y)=2n⁡(Γα​(πX​Y)+o⁡(1)),α∈[0,∞],2^{nT_{\alpha}(\pi_{XY})}=2^{n(\Gamma_{\alpha}(\pi_{XY})+o(1))},\quad\alpha\in[0,\infty],

and under Condition 1,

2n​Tα​(πX​Y)=2n⁡(1+H⁡(ϵ)−2​H​(a)+o⁡(1)),α∈[−∞,0).2^{nT_{\alpha}(\pi_{XY})}=2^{n(1+H(\epsilon)-2H(a)+o(1))},\quad\alpha\in[-\infty,0).

IV Proof of Theorem 1 for α∈[−∞,0)\alpha\in[-\infty,0)

IV-A Converse

By the monotonicity and the skew symmetry of Rényi divergence, T~α​(πX​Y)≥T~β​(πX​Y)\widetilde{T}_{\alpha}(\pi_{XY})\geq\widetilde{T}_{\beta}(\pi_{XY}) holds for any α∈[−∞,0)\alpha\in[-\infty,0) and β∈(0,1)\beta\in(0,1). Moreover, T~β​(πX​Y)=C𝖶​(πX​Y)\widetilde{T}_{\beta}(\pi_{XY})=C_{\mathsf{W}}(\pi_{XY}). The converse for α∈[−∞,0)\alpha\in[-\infty,0) follows.

IV-C Exponential Behavior

Proposition 3.
